0001| # Machine-readable client commands
0002| 
0003| Every operation of the local client is also a parameterized `forgel` subcommand
0004| that needs no interactive prompt. With `--json` a command writes exactly one
0005| JSON object to stdout and nothing else; without the flag the human-readable
0006| text is unchanged, so `forgel`, `forgel chat`, `forgel telegram` and their
0007| interactive commands keep working as before.
0008| 
0009| ## Envelope
0010| 
0011| ```json
0012| {"ok": true, "kind": "status", "text": "project-1a2b: task review (...)",
0013|  "error": "", "project": {"id": "project-1a2b", "state": "task review"}}
0014| ```
0015| 
0016| Flat top level:
0017| 
0018| | field | meaning |
0019| |---|---|
0020| | `ok` | success flag |
0021| | `kind` | `answer`, `change_request`, `action`, `plan`, `status`, `tasks`, `task`, `projects`, `session`, `use`, `history`, `control`, `daemon` |
0022| | `text` | the reply text a human would see |
0023| | `error` | empty on success, a description otherwise |
0024| | payload | one of `task` (+ `task_id`), `tasks`, `plan`, `project`, `projects`, `history`, `paused`, `cycles` |
0025| 
0026| A failed call exits non-zero and still writes one JSON object with
0027| `"ok": false` and the reason in `error`; the same reason goes to stderr. The
0028| payload never carries secrets.
0029| 
0030| ## Commands
0031| 
0032| ```text
0033| forgel say --project <id> --text "..." [--session <key>] [--json]
0034| forgel say "add a health endpoint" [--json]
0035| forgel projects [--json]
0036| forgel session [<project>] [--session <key>] [--json]
0037| forgel use <project> [--session <key>] [--json]
0038| forgel history [--session <key>] [--limit N] [--json]
0039| forgel tasks [<project>] [--json]
0040| forgel status <project> --json
0041| forgel task accept|reject|retry|cancel|add --project <id> [--task <id>] [--json]
0042| forgel plan <project> --goal "..." [--dry-run] [--json]
0043| forgel plan <project> --status --json
0044| forgel daemon [--once|--loop] [--interval S] [--max-cycles N] --json
0045| forgel pause [--json]
0046| forgel resume [--json]
0047| ```
0048| 
0049| `say` is the single free-text entry point. It calls the same `CommandRouter`
0050| as the console and Telegram and reports what the message became: an answer, a
0051| queued `change_request` task, a `plan` or a control `action`. The CLI never
0052| reimplements routing.
0053| 
0054| ## Sessions
0055| 
0056| The active project is a durable engine-side session, so the client keeps no
0057| state between calls. The session key defaults to `local` (the console chat id
0058| 0) and is switched with `--session`. `forgel session <project>` and
0059| `forgel use <project>` set it, `forgel session` reads it back,
0060| `forgel projects` marks the selected one, and `forgel history` returns the
0061| recent conversation of the session.

0001| """Console-script entry point.
0002| 
0003| ``forgel`` dispatches three kinds of work: the reporting commands that read
0004| only from the ledger (``forgel cost``), the machine-readable client commands
0005| (``forgel say``, ``forgel status --json``, ...) and everything else, which stays
0006| in ``forgel.cli``. Keeping the split here means the reporting path never has to
0007| start a model session and the client parser never changes the legacy commands.
0008| """
0009| 
0010| from __future__ import annotations
0011| 
0012| import sys
0013| from typing import Sequence
0014| 
0015| 
0016| def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
0017|     arguments = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
0018|     if arguments and arguments[0] == "cost":
0019|         from .costs import cost_command
0020| 
0021|         return cost_command(arguments[1:])
0022|     from .client import maybe_dispatch
0023| 
0024|     handled = maybe_dispatch(arguments)
0025|     if handled is not None:
0026|         return handled
0027|     from .cli import main as cli_main
0028| 
0029|     return cli_main(arguments)

0070| ## Overview
0071| 
0072| Forgel Code can currently only be obtained by cloning the repository and creating a virtual environment, which makes the first-run experience multi-step and error-prone. The milestone goal is a single-command installation, but no `install.sh` exists at the repository root, the README's installation path is not the one-command path, and there are no automated guards for either the installer behaviour or the README's installation section.
0073| 
0074| **Outcome:** A POSIX `sh` installer at the repository root installs the Forgel Code client into a per-user prefix, creates a `forgel-code` entry point on PATH via a single marked profile block, supports a profile opt-out, is safely re-runnable, can be uninstalled with a flag, and prints the installed version. The README's first and only main installation command is `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh`, with one update line, one uninstall line, the Python 3 and `forgel` engine prerequisites, and a single Windows line outside the main path. Automated tests run the real installer offline in a temporary HOME and guard the README ordering.
0075| 
0076| ## Goals
0077| 
0078| - Make Forgel Code installable and runnable with one documented command.
0079| - Keep the installation self-contained, per-user, re-runnable and reversible.
0080| - Make the single-command installation path the only documented main path, guarded by tests.
0081| 
0082| ## Non-Goals
0083| 
0084| - Any change to client behaviour, rendering, session handling or engine calls under `forgel_code/`.
0085| - Publishing to PyPI, pipx, Homebrew, apt or any other distribution channel.
0086| - A Windows-native installer (PowerShell, `.bat`); Windows stays a documented `pip install --user` fallback line.
0087| - Automatic update checking, self-update, or version pinning beyond the tag in the URL.
0088| - Installing, bundling or managing the `forgel` engine itself.
0089| - Shell profile support for shells other than the ones the installer detects from `$SHELL` (no new shell-detection framework).
0090| - CI configuration changes beyond running the existing test command.
0091|

0102| ## Functional Requirements
0103| 
0104| - **FR-1**: R1: `install.sh` exists at the repository root with the executable bit set and is valid POSIX `sh` (runs under `sh`, not only `bash`).
0105| - **FR-2**: R2: `install.sh` depends only on `sh` standard utilities and Python 3; it does not require a pre-existing virtualenv, network access when given a local source, or any package manager other than the Python tool it detects.
0106| - **FR-3**: R3: `install.sh` installs the client into `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` when set, otherwise `$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code`; installing must not require virtualenv activation.
0107| - **FR-4**: R4: `install.sh` writes an executable `forgel-code` launcher into `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` when set, otherwise `$HOME/.local/bin`; running that launcher without activation must work.
0108| - **FR-5**: R5: `install.sh` adds the bin directory to PATH exactly once, inside a block delimited by a clearly marked start and end comment, in the shell profile selected from `$SHELL` (falling back to `$HOME/.profile`); no second block is appended on re-run.
0109| - **FR-6**: R6: When the opt-out environment variable is set, `install.sh` opens no profile file for writing and instead prints exactly the `export PATH=...` line the user must add.
0110| - **FR-7**: R7: On success `install.sh` prints the installed version and exits with status 0.
0111| - **FR-8**: R8: Re-running `install.sh` over an existing installation replaces the installation, leaves exactly one PATH block, and exits with status 0.
0112| - **FR-9**: R9: `install.sh --uninstall` removes the installation directory, the `forgel-code` launcher, and the marked PATH block that the installer added, and exits with status 0.
0113| - **FR-10**: R10: `install.sh` accepts a local source tree (offline mode, e.g. via an environment variable pointing at a checkout) so the installation path can be exercised without network access.
0114| - **FR-11**: R11: `README.md`'s installation section starts with exactly the command `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh` as its first installation command, and no `pip install`, `python3 -m venv`, `pipx` or `--user` appears before it or as an alternative main path.
0115| - **FR-12**: R12: `README.md` retains the Python 3 requirement, the requirement that the `forgel` engine is on PATH including how to point at a custom engine path, exactly one update line (same command with a new tag), and exactly one uninstall line.

0122| ## Technical Requirements
0123| 
0124| - `install.sh` must be POSIX `sh` compatible and pass shell parsing/warnings under `sh -n`.
0125| - Tests must never write to the developer's real `$HOME`, real shell profile, or `~/.local`; every installer test sets `HOME` and the target/bin/profile variables to a temporary directory.
0126| - No network access is required by the test suite; the offline test must exercise the real installer, not a stub.

0128| - Documentation changes stay within the installation section plus the lines the requirements name; unrelated README content is not rewritten.
0129| - The installer must remain a single self-contained file so it can be piped through `curl ... | sh`.

0131| ## User Stories
0132| 
0133| - As a new user, I want one command that installs Forgel Code, so that I do not have to clone the repository or activate a virtualenv.
0134| - As a user with a custom shell setup, I want to opt out of profile modification, so that the installer does not edit my dotfiles and can tell me the exact line to add.
0135| - As a user upgrading to a new release, I want to re-run the same command with a new tag, so that updating is the same as installing.
0136| - As a user who no longer wants the tool, I want one uninstall command, so that the installation and the PATH line it added are gone.

0040| # The self-hosting CLI runs from its own non-editable copy: the coding agent
0041| # edits src/forgel while the daemon works, so a live import would load
0042| # half-edited modules and break the running console. Build from the committed
0043| # tree, never install with -e. Replacing the files under a running process
0044| # mixes old and new modules, so restart the console or daemon afterwards.

0046| 	@tmp=$$(mktemp -d); \
0047| 	trap 'rm -rf "$$tmp"' EXIT; \
0048| 	git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$$tmp"; \

0001| # Machine-readable client commands
0002| 
0003| Every operation of the local client is also a parameterized `forgel` subcommand
0004| that needs no interactive prompt. With `--json` a command writes exactly one
0005| JSON object to stdout and nothing else; without the flag the human-readable
0006| text is unchanged, so `forgel`, `forgel chat`, `forgel telegram` and their
0007| interactive commands keep working as before.
0008| 
0009| ## Envelope
0010| 
0011| ```json
0012| {"ok": true, "kind": "status", "text": "project-1a2b: task review (...)",
0013|  "error": "", "project": {"id": "project-1a2b", "state": "task review"}}
0014| ```
0015| 
0016| Flat top level:
0017| 
0018| | field | meaning |
0019| |---|---|
0020| | `ok` | success flag |
0021| | `kind` | `answer`, `change_request`, `action`, `plan`, `status`, `tasks`, `task`, `projects`, `session`, `use`, `history`, `control`, `daemon` |
0022| | `text` | the reply text a human would see |
0023| | `error` | empty on success, a description otherwise |
0024| | payload | one of `task` (+ `task_id`), `tasks`, `plan`, `project`, `projects`, `history`, `paused`, `cycles` |
0025| 
0026| A failed call exits non-zero and still writes one JSON object with
0027| `"ok": false` and the reason in `error`; the same reason goes to stderr. The
0028| payload never carries secrets.
0029| 
0030| ## Commands
0031| 
0032| ```text
0033| forgel say --project <id> --text "..." [--session <key>] [--json]
0034| forgel say "add a health endpoint" [--json]
0035| forgel projects [--json]
0036| forgel session [<project>] [--session <key>] [--json]
0037| forgel use <project> [--session <key>] [--json]
0038| forgel history [--session <key>] [--limit N] [--json]
0039| forgel tasks [<project>] [--json]
0040| forgel status <project> --json
0041| forgel task accept|reject|retry|cancel|add --project <id> [--task <id>] [--json]
0042| forgel plan <project> --goal "..." [--dry-run] [--json]
0043| forgel plan <project> --status --json
0044| forgel daemon [--once|--loop] [--interval S] [--max-cycles N] --json
0045| forgel pause [--json]
0046| forgel resume [--json]
0047| ```
0048| 
0049| `say` is the single free-text entry point. It calls the same `CommandRouter`
0050| as the console and Telegram and reports what the message became: an answer, a
0051| queued `change_request` task, a `plan` or a control `action`. The CLI never
0052| reimplements routing.
0053| 
0054| ## Sessions
0055| 
0056| The active project is a durable engine-side session, so the client keeps no
0057| state between calls. The session key defaults to `local` (the console chat id
0058| 0) and is switched with `--session`. `forgel session <project>` and
0059| `forgel use <project>` set it, `forgel session` reads it back,
0060| `forgel projects` marks the selected one, and `forgel history` returns the
0061| recent conversation of the session.

0001| """Runtime presets: how a repository reads and writes its version manifests.
0002| 
0003| A release version is carried by the tag and the changelog, but a repository
0004| also declares its version in runtime-specific files: ``package.json`` for
0005| Node, ``pyproject.toml`` or ``__init__.py`` for Python, a version initializer
0006| for Rails. Those files are a property of the runtime, not of the release
0007| train, so the release train asks a preset to read the current version and to
0008| write the new one.
0009| 
0010| Presets are data in the registry (``registry/recipes.json``) and a repository
0011| selects one explicitly with ``preset:`` in ``program.yaml`` or by the files it
0012| contains. An unknown explicit preset is an error; a repository with no preset
0013| keeps the tag and changelog as its only release record.
0014| """

It never pushes 0452| to the base branch and never force-pushes. `[git]` in `forgel.toml` controls 0453| the policy: 0454| 0455| ```toml 0456| [git] 0457| provider = "github" 0458| auth = "auto" # auto | github_app | pat | deploy_key 0459| base_branch = "main" 0460| branch_prefix = "forgel/" 0461| draft_pr = true 0462| require_ci = true 0463| merge = "auto" # auto | human 0464| auto_revert_on_failure = true 0465| ``` 0466| 0467| ```bash 0468| forgel github status 0469| forgel github publish --title "Add dark mode" [--repo api] [--commit "message"] 0470| forgel github merge [--pr 12] 0471| ``` 0472| 0473| ```text 0474| /github 0475| /github publish [repo] 0476| /github merge [repo] [pr] 0477| ``` 0478| 0479| `publish` fetches, rebases onto `origin/<base>` (a conflict stops the run), 0480| commits when a message is given, pushes the feature branch, opens a draft PR 0481| and records it in `docs/program/git/report.md` and the ledger. With 0482| `merge=auto` it waits for checks and merges only when they are green; with 0483| `require_ci=true` and no CI checks it stops at `no_ci`. `merge=human` leaves 0484| the pull request open. Post-merge smoke and auto-revert are not implemented 0485| yet; the config field is reserved. 0486| 0487| ## Releases 0488| 0489| Every accepted change request is a release. The agent turns the request into a 0490| release train, the planner splits it into tasks, and when every task is 0491| accepted the runtime audits the whole change set and publishes one version in 0492| each repository the request touched. A published tag is never moved: a change 0493| after a release is a new version. A request that depends on several 0494| repositories releases them together; versions still differ per repository. 0495| Before publication the runtime writes the release plan and the audit under 0496| `docs/program/releases/<release_id>/`, the repository gets `CHANGELOG.md` and 0497| `releases/<version>/{plan,release}.md`, then an annotated `v<version>` tag and 0498| the provider release are pushed. Publication retries a failed push and a 0499| missing provider release on later daemon cycles. 0500| 0501| The version comes from the repository itself. Release tags and `CHANGELOG.md` 0502| set the base; without release history the first version is `0.1.0`. A patch 0503| release increments the patch number, a minor release (new functionality or 0504| changed behaviour) the minor number. A major release is only meaningful from 0505| `1.0.0` onward: before that a breaking change is still a minor release, and 0506| `1.0.0` is the first product release. A failed audit queues fix tasks in the 0507| same release for its critical and major findings. A failure with nothing 0508| blocking publishes the release; its findings stay in the audit report. 0509| 0510| Version manifests are written by the repository's runtime preset, not by the 0511| release train. A repository selects one explicitly with `preset:` in 0512| `program.yaml`, or the runtime detects it from `pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/ 0513| `requirements.txt`/`manage.py` (Python), `package.json` (Node) or `Gemfile` 0514| (Rails). The Python preset updates static `pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg` 0515| metadata and `__version__` constants; the Node preset updates the root and 0516| `apps/*/package.json`; the Rails preset updates `API_VERSION` in 0517| `config/initializers/version.rb`. Presets are data under `presets` in the 0518| registry; a project can add its own manifest layout there and select it by id. 0519| 0520| The explicit command remains for a manual release outside the request flow. 0521| It tags every code repository at a committed SHA and, when an API token is 0522| available (GitHub App, PAT or `gh` session), creates the provider release 0523| object — a GitHub release with notes. Without a token the tag is still 0524| created and pushed; the result says `tagged` and names the fallback. 0525| 0526| ```bash 0527| forgel release <project> --version 1.2.0 [--notes "..."] [--repo api] [--draft] [--generate-notes] 0528| ``` 0529| 0530| ```text 0531| /release [--version X] [--notes ...] [--repo ID] [--draft] [--generate-notes] 0532| ``` 0533| 0534| The tag is `v<version>` for a plain SemVer (or the version as given); without 0535| `--version` it is `g<generation>`. Repositories must have no uncommitted 0536| changes; a tag that already exists at a different SHA is refused, while the 0537| same SHA is pushed idempotently. The manifest 0538| `docs/program/releases/<tag>.json` records every repository SHA, the release 0539| digest, release URLs and the staging/production approvals. 0540| `--generate-notes` asks GitHub to build the notes from commits; the default 0541| body lists the released repositories. GitHub Releases use the Contents 0542| read/write permission already required for pushing — the App needs no extra 0543| scope, a fine-grained PAT needs Contents read/write and a classic PAT needs 0544| `repo`. The installation must include the repository; without the permission 0545| the API returns a 403 and the release falls back to a tagged result. This is 0546| the release step after the human-approved staging candidate. 0547| 0548| ## Coding Agent 0549| 0550| Queue a task for a project: 0551| 0552| ```bash 0553| forgel task add <project> \ 0554| --title "Minimal blog platform" \ 0555| --require "Build a blog in Python with the standard library" \ 0556| --require "Tests run with python -m unittest discover -s tests" \ 0557| --accept "The external validator exits 0" \ 0558| --test-command "python -m unittest discover -s tests" 0559| forgel task list <project> 0560| forgel task accept <project> --task <id> [--notes "..."] 0561| forgel task reject <project> --task <id> [--notes "..."] 0562| ``` 0563| 0564| A plain chat message is not just conversation: the project agent classifies it, 0565| and a change request becomes a pending task with explicit requirements, 0566| acceptance criteria, a target repository, optional constraints, a test command 0567| and recorded assumptions. In a multi-repository project the agent picks the 0568| most likely repository and states why instead of asking; a wrong assumption is 0569| corrected by the next request. The bot reports the task id, and `/tasks` lists 0570| it. Cancel any task with `/task cancel <id>`. 0571| 0572| For a milestone, `forgel plan <project> --goal "..."` (or `/plan <goal>` in the 0573| chat) asks the planner for an ordered backlog of task intents; a separate 0574| requirements writer expands each intent into a formal specification, and a plan 0575| review checks the whole plan against the goal before queueing. `--dry-run` 0576| previews the specifications. The plan is committed as 0577| `docs/program/plans/<id>.md`, and the daemon runs the tasks in the order the 0578| plan lists them. 0579| 0580| The daemon picks up pending tasks and runs the coding agent inside the 0581| project's repository. The model returns one JSON action per turn (list, read, 0582| write, delete, run, done, fail). The runtime keeps paths inside the repository, 0583| uses a small command allowlist, strips secret environment variables, caps the 0584| step count, runs the final test command, commits with a bot message, writes 0585| `docs/program/agent/<task>.md` and records a ledger event. It refuses to commit 0586| secret-looking files. After a done task the independent QA pass runs the 0587| environment contract again (sandbox or local); a red gate fails the task and 0588| writes `docs/program/agent/<task>.qa.md`. Then an independent reviewer with a 0589| clean context judges the committed diff against the explicit requirements and 0590| writes `docs/program/agent/<task>.review.md`; a failed verdict fails the task. 0591| A passing review is accepted automatically (`FORGEL_TASK_ACCEPT=auto`, the 0592| default); `forgel task accept|reject` or `/task accept|reject` remains 0593| available for manual decisions. Set `FORGEL_TASK_ACCEPT=human` to leave every 0594| green task in `review` for a human. A review-only criterion is judged by the 0595| reviewer; only an errored review needs a human. 0596| 0597| Every failure goes to the controlling agent: it sees the failing command, its 0598| exit code and its output, and decides whether to retry, send the work back 0599| with feedback (`FORGEL_TASK_REWORKS=8`), fix a broken check or limit, or stop 0600| and ask a human. An exhausted budget fails the task; with 0601| `FORGEL_PLAN_ON_FAILURE=stop` the rest of its milestone stops too. When a review 0602| rejection repeats, an external arbiter decides whether the change or the 0603| acceptance criteria are wrong; `criteria` fails the task with a proposed 0604| revision. `forgel task retry` requeues a failed task and releases the tasks its 0605| milestone stopped; `forgel plan --status` shows the milestone state. 0606| 0607| Tasks carry executable acceptance checks, run by QA and stored outside the 0608| agent's write scope. A criterion that cannot be automated is marked 0609| `verification: review` and judged by the independent reviewer. Tests are 0610| normally only added; a deletion needs a recorded reason (`removed`, `replaced` 0611| with the replacement, or `wrong`), and an unjustified deletion fails the 0612| review. 0613| 0614| From the chat: send a plain message to the selected project to queue a change; 0615| `/plan` decomposes a milestone; `/tasks` shows the queue; `/task accept|reject` 0616| records a review decision; `/task cancel <id>` cancels a task in any status — 0617| it leaves the task list, its requirements document is marked cancelled at the 0618| top and is never accepted for work again, and commits it already made stay in 0619| the tree for the release audit to judge. 0620| 0621| Free local runs can use a scripted model or a subagent bridge instead of a 0622| provider key; a production run uses `FORGEL_MODEL_API_KEY`. The manual blog e2e 0623| and its acceptance criteria are in [tests/e2e/README.md](tests/e2e/README.md); 0624| it is run on explicit instruction and not part of `make test`. 0625| 0626| ## Project Layout 0627| 0628| A local adoption links the folder in place: 0629| 0630| ``` 0631| my-repo/ the source folder — the single source of truth 0632| forgel.toml process config (committed) 0633| program.yaml repository graph (committed) 0634| FORGEL.md · AGENTS.md process canon (committed) 0635| docs/program/... features, tasks, plans, QA/review evidence (committed) 0636| .forgel/ gitignored local state only 0637| project.json layout, mode, repository ids and paths 0638| conversation.jsonl · agent-home/ · staging.json 0639| README.md · src/ · ... the product, untouched and shared with your tools 0640| ``` 0641| 0642| The process artifacts are part of the repository history; `.forgel` is local 0643| state and is never committed. `program.yaml` points at the repository with a 0644| relative path (`.` for the folder itself). No copy of the code exists. 0645| 0646| Remote adoption and template projects use a container: 0647| 0648| ``` 0649| project/ 0650| project.json machine state: layout, mode, repository ids 0651| program/ control repository 0652| repos/ 0653| api/ web/ infra/ e2e/ one real git repository each 0654| ``` 0655| 0656| Every repository has its own history and a `forgel-baseline` tag. External 0657| changes, rollback and the complexity patch are computed per repository and 0658| aggregated into one project report. Existing M0 projects keep the flat layout 0659| and remain readable. 0660| 0661| Deploy it from your laptop with one command: 0662| 0663| ```bash 0664| forgel deploy init # creates .env.deploy 0665| $EDITOR .env.deploy 0666| forgel deploy up 0667| ``` 0668| 0669| The utility reads `.env.deploy`, talks to the server over SSH, builds the image 0670| remotely or pushes it to a registry, uploads the production Compose file and a 0671| `0600` runtime `.env`, starts the service and runs the doctor. The server needs 0672| only SSH, Docker and Compose: if they are missing, the utility warns and asks 0673| permission to install (root or passwordless sudo); otherwise it prints the 0674| manual commands. Edit the same file and run `forgel deploy up` to change 0675| configuration; `status`, `logs`, `restart` and `backup` are available too. 0676| Image publishing to GHCR is optional; see [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md). 0677| 0678| The manual Compose path is still available: 0679| 0680| ```bash 0681| cp .env.example .env # set the token and your chat id 0682| docker compose --profile telegram up -d --build telegram 0683| ``` 0684| 0685| The bot and the ledger share the `/data` volume, so state survives restarts. 0686| The daemon runs from the image; stopping the process is a deployment action, 0687| not a chat command. 0688| 0689| ## Configuration 0690| 0691| - `forgel.toml` — project config: QA runtime, jurisdiction pack, model policy, context window, peak policy, budget. 0692| - `environment.yaml` — the project environment contract: image or build, the `setup`, `test`, `e2e` commands Forgel runs, and optional `env`. It sits in the control repository, or in the repository itself for a single-repository project. The core carries no per-language commands. See `PLAN.md` §7.13. 0693| - `FORGEL.md` → `AGENTS.md` → `CLAUDE.md` — instruction files, read in that order. 0694| - `forgel config <project-id>` — show the effective project config. 0695| - `forgel context <project-id> [--raw]` — show the resolved context files and their priority. 0696| - `forgel doctor` — check the home, registry, ledger, Telegram, model, GitHub and tools before a deployment. See [docs/deploy.md](docs/deploy.md). 0697| 0698| ## Edit Outside Forgel 0699| 0700| Forgel never regenerates or overwrites external work. After editing a generated 0701| project by hand or in another harness: 0702| 0703| ```bash 0704| forgel sync <project-id> 0705| forgel run <project-id> 0706| ``` 0707| 0708| `sync` records the diff in `docs/program/external-changes.md` and 0709| `docs/program/reconciliation.md`, then asks for a decision: 0710| 0711| ```bash 0712| forgel reconcile <project-id> --decision accept|fix|rollback|ignore [--notes "..."] 0713| ``` 0714| 0715| - `accept` — document the change in the feature spec. 0716| - `fix` — keep it as a defect; the pipeline blocks at review until it is fixed. 0717| - `rollback` — restore the changed files from the generated baseline. 0718| - `ignore` — record the change and continue without documenting it. 0719| 0720| Only then does `forgel run` continue, in a new ledger generation, from `review`. 0721| 0722| For a brownfield project, reconcile does not start the template pipeline: 0723| `accept` and `ignore` commit the accepted changes to the repository baseline, 0724| `rollback` restores the files, and `fix` records the defect. The same decisions 0725| are available from the chat with `/sync` and `/reconcile`. 0726| 0727| ## What it will do 0728| 0729| - Chat interface (Telegram) → requirements → a validated recipe (stack + cloud + integrations). 0730| - Multi-repo project: backend, frontend, infrastructure, E2E. 0731| - Spec-driven development with clean-context roles: spec writer, developer, reviewer, QA, acceptor. 0732| - Independent end-to-end QA and acceptance evidence — not "the agent said it works". 0733| - Jurisdiction packs: legal constraints become default requirements and evidence — not a document attached at the end.
